messages.author: 1aac3a0c0458ace2
messages.subject: pcount vs occuRN
parts:
Dear unmarked users,

I have a simple question: how to assess which type of model (Royle Biometrics or Royle-Nichols) is the better choice for my dataset?

I am trying to estimate bear abundance using track counts on 2-km stretches of forest roads in the Carpathians. There are 36 transects with 4 visits per transect. There are a lot of zeroes, and the track counts are low, ranging between 1 and 3 (mostly 1s). The occuRN models use the count data truncated to 1s.

So far I used model averaging for sets of pcount and occuRN models separately, and I obtain slightly different estimates of abundance. Can I select which models perform better by just comparing AIC values of occuRN and pcount models? I am basically using the same dataset for both types of models, but I was not sure if using AIC to compare across different types of models is correct.  

Thank you...

Best,
Viorel

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcount vs occuRN
parts:
Dear Viorel,
 you should use the pcount() function which fits the N-mixture model.  It probably isn't possible to compare the AIC because the likelihoods are scaled differently between the two models. In any case, the RN model assumes a binary observation whereas the N-mixture model the observation has support 0,1,2,3,...., which matches up with your situation.
regards
andy

messages.author: a6a37ee1eb02de16
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] pcount vs occuRN
parts:
Just one question regarding the data of Viroel. Maybe further details about the abundance estimation that Viorel wish to do are needed; although maybe I'm not correct.

If he want to calculate bear abundance as no. of bears (or something similar), I think that he should take only presence/absence [0,1] of tracks in the transects and then use occuRN to estimate abundance (or whatever lambda should be interpreted as). Otherwise, using pcount() with track counts (no. of tracks per transect) will result in an estimation of the no. of tracks rather than the number of bears (that will require further assumptions to be derived from the track counts as no. of tracks leaved behind by each individual, etc).

Am I right with my interpretation?

Pablo

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcount vs occuRN
parts:
If the count is the number of unique individuals then pcount() is appropriate for estimating mean abundance.
If you're counting the number of tracks, as suggested by Pablo, then I agree, the model would produce something similar to an estimate of the population size of tracks (even that is questionable because tracks are not independent samples of anything!).

If it is not possible to deduce unique individuals, then reduce the data to simple presence/absence and use the RN model.

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] pcount vs occuRN
parts:
Dear Pablo,

yes, you are right if what he counts is the number of tracks. However, I have seen people doing snow transects and trying to only count the number of unique animals that left a track. I don't know how practical that is but if this is possible, then of course the counts refer to individual animals and the abundance estimate to the total number of animals associated with the area that is sampled by the transect.

Regards  --  Marc
